ks1.objective: Carry or roll a football through a field of 'defenders' — beat as many as you can while moving safely across the pitch.
successCriteria: Moves through the area without bumping into cones
Counts how many defenders they beat
Tries to travel the full length of the pitch

lks2.objective: Dribble around scattered cone defenders using changes of direction and speed. Progress from carrying the ball to dribbling with the feet.
successCriteria: Dribbles with head up to see the next 'defender'
Uses different parts of the foot to change direction
Beats defenders using speed changes or feints

uks2.objective: Take on live and static defenders in a 1v1-heavy environment. Use step-overs, feints and changes of pace to beat opponents cleanly under pressure.
successCriteria: Executes at least one recognisable skill move to beat a defender
Maintains close control at speed under pressure
Chooses when to attack and when to reset — reads the space

space.description: Rectangular pitch marked with large cones at the corners. Scatter small cones across the pitch to represent the 'Marc Guéhi' defenders — spread them out but leave clear routes to weave through. Roughly 25×15m for 15 children.

ks1.description: Smaller pitch (18×12m) with fewer, more widely spaced defender cones. Keep it obvious and forgiving.

uks2.description: Larger pitch (30×18m) with defenders packed more tightly to force quick decisions. Add target goals at one end.

value.name: Bravery
value.text: Taking on a defender is a brave choice — especially in front of teammates. Praise the decision to attack the space, not just the moment it works. Name the children who try a feint, chase a rebound, or go again after being tackled. Bravery is the willingness to try, not the guarantee of success.

steps: Set up the pitch with large corner cones. Scatter small cones across the area to represent 'Marc Guéhi' defenders.
Every child starts at one end with a football.
Children travel across the area, aiming to 'beat' as many defenders (cones) as possible by getting close and moving past.
Start with the football carried in hands so children learn the routes and rhythm.
Progress to dribbling the football with the feet — same task, higher control demand.
Once children reach the far end, they turn and go back — count defenders beaten each trip.
Every minute or so, pause and share the highest counts. Praise the routes children chose.
progressions: Begin by challenging children to move around the area holding the football, beating as many defenders as possible.
Encourage children to shout out their favourite World Cup player's name after beating 5 defenders.
Challenge children to 'trick' the defenders by pretending to move one way before quickly changing direction and going the other way.
Progress so children dribble the football with the feet while beating the defenders.
Select some children to become live defenders — they stand next to selected cones without a football and try to intercept.
questions: Which route did you choose — and why?
What did you do when a defender was right in front of you?
What's the difference between beating a cone and beating a live defender?
Which World Cup player do you play like when you're being brave on the ball?

step.space: Reduce the gaps between defending cones to force quicker decisions and tighter ball control; widen them to let children build confidence.
step.task: Challenge children to perform a specific turn, step-over or skill move before beating a defender.
step.equipment: Add target goals around the area — children must beat a defender before finishing into a goal. Change from cones to poles for tighter dribbling.
step.people: Pair or group children of similar ability against live defenders to keep 1v1s realistic. Rotate defender and attacker roles regularly.

base.showmanship: Bring energy and excitement into the session by comparing the children to the world's best attackers competing at the FIFA World Cup. Call out the skill moves by name — 'that's a Guéhi-beater right there!' — and make each successful move feel like a highlight-reel moment.

steps: Set up a small pitch. Scatter a small number of cones across as 'defenders'.
Every child starts with a football at one end.
Carry the football and move around the cones without touching them.
Count how many defenders you got past — try to beat your own score next time.
progressions: Start with the football in hands.
Progress to rolling the ball with the feet slowly.
Encourage children to keep their head up to see the next defender.
questions: How many did you beat this time?
What do you look for before you move?
Which was your favourite way to get past?

coachingCard.objective: Beat defenders 1v1, change direction, attack space.
coachingCard.setup: Grid, ball each, scattered cone defenders with clear gaps.
coachingCard.idea: I: You're taking on Marc Guéhi! D: Show approach, fake and accelerate. E: Beat as many defenders as possible. A: Play.
coachingCard.observation: Are players committing the defender before changing direction?
coachingCard.cues: Head up · Small touches · Slow then go · Explode into space.
coachingCard.interventions: ~3 mins: coaching point. ~7 mins: progression. ~11 mins: final challenge.
coachingCard.progressions: Dribble instead of carry · Specific turns · Live defenders · Beat defender then score through gate.
coachingCard.differentiation: Bigger gaps, free dribble (support). Weaker foot, specific moves, live defenders (stretch).
coachingCard.behaviourSafety: Spread out · Different defenders · Head up · Avoid collisions.
coachingCard.finishReflect: Finish: How many defenders can you beat in one minute? Reflect: 'What helped you beat the defender?' 'When did you change direction?'
